specs.scene: An overhead flat-lay of a barbershop's front counter, an open appointment ledger beside a corded phone cradle, scissors and combs fanned across the laminate, a cash drawer half open with loose bills, a stack of blank appointment cards, a barber's hands entering from the bottom edge tidying the ledger, bare patches of counter left open between the tools.
specs.source_quote: Companies too small for Culture Amp bleed this quietly

recognisable.why: a barbershop counter is an instantly familiar small-business trade, no label needed.

legibility.why: the counter reads as one working surface even though many small props sit on it, consistent with the flatlay convention.

curiosity.why: the overlay implies loss but states it plainly rather than leaving a verdict genuinely unresolved.

subject.why: the counter with hands present anchors the frame, though it is a scattered surface rather than one single object.

credible.why: no figure appears anywhere in the frame.

stakes.why: losing staff at a small shop is a direct threat to the viewing owner's own business.

reexpress.why: the shop-floor consequence is new information the title options never state.

specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a person seen from behind carrying a cardboard box of personal belongings through a glass office lobby toward the exit doors, the lobby surfaces blank and slightly out of focus around them.
specs.source_quote: the moment you watched one strong person leave a team you ran

recognisable.why: someone walking out with a box is an immediately understood, widely familiar image of quitting.

legibility.why: one figure with one object forms a single resolvable mass.

curiosity.why: the caption states a fact but leaves the consequence — who covers the work, for how long — unresolved and wanted.

subject.why: a person mid-action is a clean, undeniable anchor.

credible.why: no figure is carried, satisfying the full-credit no-number condition.

stakes.why: the image implies direct loss to whoever is left running the team.

reexpress.why: it dramatizes the human moment behind the title's dollar or market framing rather than repeating it.

specs.scene: A single printed spreadsheet page filling the frame edge to edge, dense grid lines and columns of numbers, a yellow highlighter resting diagonally across one corner, the paper curled slightly at the edges, the surface beneath left blank.
specs.source_quote: The methodology lives in a spreadsheet, which costs nothing

recognisable.why: a gridded spreadsheet page is a universally recognized office object needing no explanation.

legibility.why: the page is the sole object filling the frame, one mass to resolve.

curiosity.why: the overlay reads as a settled statement of fact rather than a verdict the viewer wants to chase.

subject.why: the spreadsheet is a distinct single object, though a page of numbers is a softer anchor than a person or tool.

credible.why: no figure appears; the frame carries none.

stakes.why: low-cost tooling matters to an aspiring operator-viewer but is not a direct threat or loss.

reexpress.why: it reveals the mechanism behind the practice, information none of the titles state.

specs.scene: A café owner standing behind the counter mid-conversation, holding a single printed report at chest height and looking at it, an idle espresso machine and stacked cups visible on the counter behind them, the left half of the frame left as clear open counter space.
specs.source_quote: the owner is the buyer, and what they are really buying is attrition insurance

recognisable.why: a café counter and owner is an everyday, instantly placed small-business setting.

legibility.why: the owner and report form the main mass, though the espresso machine behind adds a second element to register.

curiosity.why: the phrase implies a claim about staff staying that cannot be verified by looking, prompting the viewer to want the mechanism.

subject.why: a person mid-action holding a report is a clear, undiluted human anchor.

credible.why: no figure is carried in the overlay or scene.

stakes.why: the idea of proof against staff loss speaks directly to the viewing owner's own risk.

reexpress.why: it shows the buyer's motive rather than restating any title's cost or market claim.
